start.text:
Sergeant Gehrman is standing where he has evidently been standing for some hours.

'You'd be Blackthorn's. Smith said he'd send someone and I said I'd not stop him.' He looks at you a moment longer than the sentence needed. 'Moretti. That's a name I wrote down eight days ago.'

choices.text: Did anyone hear anything the night before?
I'd like the key to the cash box.

morning.text:
'Half seven. Door fast, shutters up, and a Miss Gerard on the stair saying nobody had seen him since Sunday. We took the frame off rather than the bolt, because I wanted the bolt kept as it was.'

He says the last part slowly, as a man who has been overruled before and would like it in the record this time.

night.text: 'Two of the neighbours heard the cathedral ring eleven and both say his light was already out. The surgeon says midnight.' He lets that stand a second. 'I'm police. I write what the surgeon says. I don't have to like the arithmetic.'

keys_ask.text:
'The box stays sealed until the estate's settled. That's the form of it.'

He says it the way a man says a thing he would rather be argued out of.

choices.text: Offer him something for his trouble.
Suggest, gently, that he wants to hand it over.

keys_paid.text:
The coins go into his glove without either of you looking at them.

'Back before dark. And Moretti — if you find something the surgeon missed, you bring it to me before you bring it to the Church.'

keys_pressed.text:
He hands it over before he has finished deciding to, and then stands there holding the shape of an objection he can no longer find.

You put the key in your pocket. He will remember this conversation wrongly for a week, and after that he will remember it correctly, and you will not be able to do anything about that.

start.text:
Naya Gerard has not sat down since you arrived.

'They said his heart. He is twenty-six. He came fourth in the mile at the spring meeting.' Her hands are flat on the table and she keeps them there deliberately. 'You were at the gathering. You know what he read out.'

choices.text: Tell me about the last week.
What did he bring into this house?

week.text:
'He stopped going out. He nailed the shutters himself — I heard him doing it, on the Thursday, and when I knocked he talked to me through the door about the weather.'

'He said the word *sincerity* to me twice and would not explain it, and I have not been able to stop thinking about that.'

pledge.text: 'A book. Notes, he called them, in a hand that wasn't his — he was very proud that it wasn't his.' She looks at the ceiling. 'He said he had it off a gentleman in the lower market and that it was older than the Kingdom, which I told him was a thing men say.'

cass.text:
'Kohler?' Something crosses her face and she folds it away. 'He was here more than the rest of us. He asked to see the notes twice in one evening.'

'He asked me at the funeral whether the police had taken anything out of the rooms. Not whether they had found anything. Whether they had taken anything.'

start.text:
Kohler Fels is talking before you have finished sitting down, and has been awake a day and a half.

'Terrible. Terrible business. I said to him, Welch, you don't read a thing like that out loud in a room, and he laughed at me — you were there, you heard him laugh.'

choices.text: The last ferry over the Tussock is at seven.
Whose hand cut the page out of his notebook?
Read what he is not saying.

alibi.text:
'Left at nine. Straight over the water to my lodgings, and I passed the lamplighter on the bridge road and a woman with two dogs, and you may ask them both.'

He offers the dogs before anybody has asked for anything.

broken.text:
You put the ferryman's hours to him, plainly, and watch him arrive at the end of the sentence a little after you do.

He starts three answers. The third one is 'I may be wrong about the day,' and he hears himself say it.

ledger.text:
'He *lent* it me. He lent it to half the faculty, he was showing it about like a dog with a hat—'

His voice goes up half a step and stays there. 'One page. One page out of a book he had no right to and everybody knew he had no right to it.'

read.text:
You ask the one thing he has spent all night preparing not to be asked, and it lands somewhere behind his eyes.

What comes back is not the answer. It is the cellar: cold at his back, coal in his hands, and above him, through the boards, a voice that had stopped being Welch's some minutes before it stopped.

bye.text: He nods too many times and goes back to not sleeping.

start.text:
Sil Mowbray is coiling a wet rope badly and in no hurry.

'Ferry's done. Ferry's done at seven, same as it's been done at seven since my father had the licence.'

choices.text: Who's been buying odd things off the market?

ferry.text:
The coins vanish into the rope coil.

'Seven, and that's the summer table. No bridge nearer than Halworth, four mile up. A man on the far bank at nine got there before seven or he got there wet.'

vane.text:
'Gentleman calls himself Aldous. Three month now. Buys paper — old paper, and not the pretty sort. Pays in notes and never haggles, which round here is a thing people notice.'

'Word was he wanted one page out of something. One page. Stopped asking Wednesday.'

halloway.text:
'The young gentleman with the shutters?' He spits over the side, unhurried. 'Come down here twice in a fortnight asking after the tide tables and the deep water. Not for a boat. For the depth.'

'Man wants to know how deep a thing goes, he's thinking about putting something in it.'

bye.text: He goes back to ruining the rope.
